Driving rules, observations, and the limits of this experiment

The fleet keeps left, follows assigned lanes without lane changes, stays below a 50 km/h limit, follows lead vehicles, stops for signals, and prioritizes pedestrians and dogs in crossings. There are no vehicle junctions, overtaking maneuvers, or emergency vehicles in this version. These are explicit simulation rules—not every road rule and not a definition of morality.

The neural policy observes speed, actual wheel angle, lane/heading error, local road geometry, desired speed, front gap and leader speed, stop distance and signal requirement, vulnerable-user conflict, and physical braking/headway margins. It uses perfect simulator observations, not a camera or learned perception. Cars use a Frenet bicycle model with independent states; actor movement and signal cycles are scripted. A separate optional supervisor may change braking, and its interventions are visible.

The bundled weights were trained with PyTorch/Adam from expert-labelled traffic states and multi-car expert rollouts. Browser continuation uses TensorFlow.js in a worker. Importing a model or completing training resets the fleet so sessions do not mix policies. This is a traffic-learning sandbox; measured rule compliance does not certify real-world safety or universal ethical behavior.
